text: A federal judge ordered one man to pay back more than eight hundred sixty-seven thousand dollars to seniors who got scammed.
It starts with a phone call. The voice on the line says it's their grandchild, or sometimes a lawyer.
Their loved one has been arrested after a car accident and needs bail money. They're also told there's a gag order, so they can't tell anyone.
They pack thousands of dollars in cash and ship it to an address the callers give them.

One man collecting that cash comes from New York City. He travels to pick it up in places like Rhode Island. In January twenty twenty-one, police in New Haven, Connecticut start getting reports from other states, and the FBI joins in.
He pleads guilty to mail fraud and conspiracy. In February twenty twenty-four, a federal judge sentences him to thirty months in federal prison.
If a caller says a relative is in jail and needs cash right now, and asks you to keep it quiet, hang up. Call your family on a number you already know. Follow for Caught number two.
